deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X_1, X_2, X_3 are the levels 1, 2, 3 of a symmetric (pre)simplicial set, i.e. a functor on non-empty finite sets {1..n}, truncated at n ≤ 3.
- The symmetric group S_n acts on X_n.
- X_1 = {e_1} is a single point (the one-vertex case).
- e_2 ∈ X_2 and e_3 ∈ X_3 are the totally degenerate elements.
- d : X_2 → X_3 is the degeneracy induced by the surjection {1,2,3} → {1,2}, 3 ↦ 2.
- p : X_3 → X_2 is the face induced by the inclusion {1,2} ⊂ {1,2,3}.

Guiding model. Take X_n = E^n with E = {x} (so the 'diagonal' collapses to e_2). Then:
- d(x,y) = (x,y,y) and p(x,y,z) = (x,y).
- ρ is the 3-cycle (x,y,z) ↦ (y,z,x).
- σ_1, σ_2, σ_3 are the transpositions fixing the 1st, 2nd and 3rd coordinate respectively.
- S_3 has the presentation ρ³ = 1, σ_i² = 1, ρσ_iρ⁻¹ = σ_{i+1}.

Boxed identities (*), read off from the model:
- pd = id
- pρd = constant map with value e_2
- pρ²d = σ
- σ_1 d = d
- pσ_3 = σp

Goal. Describe the sub-S_3-set X_3' = S_3·d(X_2), the 'degenerate part' of X_3.
- Since S_3 = {1,ρ,ρ²}·{1,σ_1} and σ_1 d = d, we get X_3' = ∪_i ρ^i d(X_2).
- Key lemma: ρ^i d(ξ) = ρ^{i'} d(ξ') implies either (i ≡ i' mod 3 and ξ = ξ') or ξ = ξ' = e_2.
- Reduce to d(ξ') = ρ^j d(ξ) and apply p.
  - j = 0: ξ' = ξ.
  - j = 1: ξ' = pρd(ξ) = e_2. So ρd(ξ) = d(e_2) = e_3, hence d(ξ) = e_3 (e_3 is S_3-fixed), hence ξ = pd(ξ) = pe_3 = e_2.
  - j = 2: ξ' = pρ²d(ξ) = σξ. So dσ(ξ) = ρ²d(ξ), hence d(ξ) = ρdσ(ξ), hence ξ = pρd(σξ) = e_2, and then ξ' = e_2.

Conclusion (drawn on the next page):
- e_3 is the unique fixed point of X_3'.
- For ξ ≠ e_2, the stabilizer of d(ξ) contains σ_1 but not ρ, so it is exactly {1,σ_1}; the orbit has 3 elements.
- Distinct ξ give distinct orbits. Note ξ and σξ give different orbits: (x,y,y) versus (y,x,x).
- Hence X_3' ≅ {e_3} ⊔ (S_3 ×_{⟨σ_1⟩} X_2^*), with X_2^* = X_2 \ {e_2}.

The next page then turns to the non-degenerate part X_3^* = X_3 \ X_3', with p^* σ_3 = σ p^*, and to surjectivity of (p, pρ) : X_3 → X_2 × X_2.

What it serves. This is an Eilenberg–Zilber-type decomposition (degenerate versus non-degenerate simplices) for low-dimensional symmetric simplicial sets with one vertex. It is presumably a step toward an algebraic description of such objects by (X_2, σ, e_2, X_3^*, p^*, ...) within the 'topos stratifié' notes.
errors: Several facts used in the argument are not listed in the box (*): e_3 = d(e_2), e_3 is S_3-invariant (needed for ρd(ξ) = e_3 ⇒ d(ξ) = e_3), pe_3 = e_2, and σe_2 = e_2 (needed at the end of the j = 2 case). All hold in the intended setting.
dσ(ξ) = ρ²d(ξ) in the j = 2 case is the case hypothesis, not a general identity. In the model, dσ(x,y) = (y,x,x) ≠ (y,x,y) = ρ²d(x,y), as the previous page records.

The next page's wording 'orbites de cardinal 3 (dans l'opposition régulière de S_3)' is inaccurate: these orbits are S_3/{1,σ_1}, not regular orbits (regular orbits would have 6 elements). The formula S_3 ×_{{1,σ_1}} X_2^* that follows is correct.

ideas.what: Normal-form identities between the degeneracy d, the face p and the S_3-action in low degrees of a symmetric simplicial set with one vertex.
ideas.modern_name: symmetric simplicial sets (presheaves on FinSet_{≥1}); simplicial identities in the category of finite sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; symmetric simplicial sets studied by Grandis, Rosický and others
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses various test categories including finite sets; unsure about this specific computation

ideas.what: Decomposition of the degenerate part of X_3 as {e_3} ⊔ S_3 ×_{⟨σ_1⟩} X_2^*, with a unique fixed point and all other orbits of type S_3/⟨σ_1⟩.
ideas.modern_name: Eilenberg–Zilber lemma for EZ-categories / generalized Reedy categories (here FinSet)

missed.claim: The page starts an explicit algebraic description of one-vertex, low-dimensional symmetric (pre)simplicial sets by degenerate/non-degenerate splitting. The intended classification of the non-degenerate part (X_3^*, p^*, with p^*σ_3 = σp^*) is only begun on the next page.
missed.quote: et on a une explicitation des struct. pré-simpliciales sur X_3' via les formules (*)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It is a concrete instance of the Eilenberg–Zilber decomposition for symmetric sets, which is well understood. Only the specific purpose within 'topos stratifié' might be of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, correct elementary computation: an Eilenberg–Zilber-type orbit decomposition for 3-simplices of a one-vertex symmetric simplicial set. It contains nothing beyond standard knowledge; its only interest is as context for the stratified-topos notes.
transcription_corrections: The circled '(4)' at the top is Grothendieck's page number. The letterhead (Académie d'Aix-Marseille, Inspection académique de Vaucluse) is printed stationery, not mathematical content.
In the line 'S_3 = {1,σ_1}.{1,ρ,ρ²} = {1,ρ,ρ²}.{1,σ_1}', the two factors on the right are underbraced and labelled roughly 'G' and 'H' (handwriting unclear); a crossed-out attempt precedes {1,σ_1}.
The parenthetical alternative in the key lemma reads 'ou [ξ = ξ' = e_2]', placed above '[ξ = ξ']' as an alternative conclusion.
The equivalent reformulation under the ⇕ is written roughly as [d(ξ) = ρ^{i'-i} d(ξ*)], with ξ* standing for ξ'; the machine version 'd(ξ') = ρ^{i-i'} d(ξ)' is equivalent.
In the j = 1 branch the sequence is: ξ' = pρd(ξ) = e_2; donc e_3 = ρd(ξ) [since d(ξ') = d(e_2) = e_3]; donc d(ξ) = e_3; ξ = pd(ξ) = pe_3 = e_2; donc ξ = ξ' = e_2.
